---
title: "Total ME inequalities for nominal independent variables"
subtitle: "Example 5.3 of Mize and Han (2025), in R"
---

With a nominal outcome *and* nominal independent variables there are two
layers of summary. On each outcome category, the effect of a nominal predictor
is its ME inequality -- the average absolute difference in that category's
probability across the predictor's groups. The Total ME inequality then sums
those across the outcome categories and halves the sum. Here race-ethnicity
and degree, both nominal, predict self-rated health. The same example in Stata
is on the [`totalme` page](/software/totalme/examples/inequalities.qmd).

## Load and prepare the data

::: {.r-run}
```r
library(haven)           # Read Stata data
library(marginaleffects) # Marginal effects and hypotheses
library(nnet)            # Multinomial logit

source("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tdmize/Rfunctions/main/ME_helper_functions.R")

gss <- read_dta("https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/cda_gss.dta")
gss <- gss[gss$year >= 2000 & gss$year <= 2021, ]

vars <- c("healthR", "race4", "age", "woman", "parent", "married", "faminc", "degree")
gss <- gss[complete.cases(gss[vars]), vars]

fvars <- c("healthR", "race4", "woman", "parent", "married", "degree")
gss[fvars] <- lapply(gss[fvars], as_factor)
nrow(gss)
```
```{.r-output}
[1] 19292
```
:::

## Fit the multinomial logit model

```r
healthmod <- multinom(healthR ~ race4 + age + woman + parent +
  married + faminc + degree, data = gss, trace = FALSE)
```

## Total ME inequalities

List the predictors in `variables`; `totalme()` returns the Total ME
inequality of each:

::: {.r-run}
```r
avg_comparisons(healthmod,
  variables = list(race4 = "pairwise", degree = "pairwise"),
  hypothesis = totalme(healthmod))
```
```{.r-output}
   Term Estimate Std. Error     z Pr(>|z|)     S  2.5 % 97.5 %
 degree   0.1157    0.00554 20.89   <0.001 319.6 0.1049 0.1266
 race4    0.0471    0.00679  6.94   <0.001  37.9 0.0338 0.0604

Type: probs
```
:::

Degree moves much more probability across the health categories than
race-ethnicity does. The weights count each pairwise comparison in proportion
to the share of the sample in the two groups compared. For the unweighted
version, which gives every comparison the same weight, use
`totalme(healthmod, weighted = FALSE)`.
